history.notes:
B3 depth-of-n, option (a), branch refactor/depth-of-n @7d3a294 vs base 9cd29d5. Every rubric item holds; checked by running, not from the reports.

FAILED ITEMS: none.

RUBRIC, item by item (reviewer's own runs):
1. PASS. Full suite on the branch: 1193 passed, 38 skipped, 5 deselected, 1 xfailed (205 s). The one xfail is KNOWN_ISSUES orientation_reversing_case_builds.
2. PASS. I ran the base src (git archive 9cd29d5) against the branch tests/. 6(a) test_pip_bearing_child_is_kept FAILS. 6(c) test_pip_depth_is_the_registered_orbit FAILS with AttributeError. 6(b), both proximity-guard variants, the default test, the TE's new test and test_pip_orbit_never_shallower x5 pass (2 failed, 10 passed).
3. PASS. git diff --stat 9cd29d5: exactly the five planned files, 237+/50- = 287 lines (cap 300). Most of the Blast.py count is the child loop moved out one indentation level.
4. PASS on the reports. The coder and the TE each measured all 11 LAW_CASES fingerprints with an independent canonicalisation, and both found base equal to branch. I did not repeat this; rubric 5/6 below and the reorder check cover the same code path.
5/6. PASS, spot-checked on two series. k28_series and nested_outer_series: every SeriesStep field, canonical JSON with addresses stripped, is byte-identical on base and branch. pip_depth is k28 [1..8, 8] and nested_outer [1..9, 9, 9, 9], equal to the plan's table.
7. PASS. One blast_zone(nested_outer largest zone, num_iterations=11, fixed_point=[fp], min_separation=1e-4): base ends at composed depth 7 (too_close 76); branch ends at composed depth 9 with result.pip_depth[fp] == 9 (too_close 78).
8. PASS. Blast.py:434-447 runs the seen check, then the exterior check, then pip_end, then the separation test as an elif. forward_depth appears only in the _pip_orbits docstring (Blast.py:116). The rubric-7 call logs exactly 8 exemption INFO lines, one per child ending at f^2..f^9(q0), no duplicates.
9. PASS. The min_separation docstring says the guard 'never decides the depth of T(q0)' and names the exemption. BlastResult documents too_close, already_known and pip_depth.
10. PASS, read as 'no new logging statement and no change outside section 5'. The diff adds exactly one logger call. Note for the author: in the rubric-7 call the branch also fires two EXISTING TangleWorkbench WARNINGs that base does not fire.
   - '361 same-stability polyline crossing(s) of the new image bridges in the tangle region', including the exempted f^9 child (258, 259);
   - '1 of 494 detections are not crossings of N', ratio 1.775, the (ii) stall point.
   They follow from section 5's intended change: the call now reaches depth 9 by keeping curve the guard used to drop. But they show that the exemption brings back near-coincident polygon artifacts, which is what the guard exists to stop. The coder's report ('No other log line was added or changed') is true of the code but leaves this out; the TE caught it. This does not move the grade; it should reach the author with the merge request.

BREAK-IT CHECKS (re-run on scratch copies; the worktree was not touched):
- Break 6, exemption moved before the exterior check: test_exemption_skips_only_the_separation_test FAILS (an exterior child at (15.20, 4.15) was kept).
- Break 1, pip_end = None: 6(a) FAILS.

CODER DEVIATIONS (all accepted):
- Pip id via registry.find(chosen) instead of the stored .id. Correct: it is the same lookup TangleSession._restore_strong_pip uses, and a stored id can go stale after a recompute without preserve_ids. The test side (cases._pip_depth and both test helpers) does the same.
- No cycle guard in the orbit walk. Correct under house style. A strong pip is not periodic and the iterate table is an asserted partial bijection, so a chain from a non-anchor cannot enter a cycle. A guard would model a state the invariants rule out.
- 6(b) finds the child by rule on its own build, not by carrying the id pair from (a). Better than the plan: no id crosses builds and none is pinned.
- Proximity test parametrized pip / no_pip, with too_close > 0 asserted only in no_pip. This is what plan step 5 asks for, and break 5 in the evidence shows no_pip goes red when the guard is disabled.
- Child filter moved after all parents of the iteration are mapped. Verified it cannot change which children are kept:
  (a) by reading: the filter mutates only local state (seen, kept_points, the step lists), so iterate_bridge never sees it and 'produced' is the same list in the same order. kept_points therefore grows in the same order, and sibling comparisons see the same predecessors.
  (b) the one workbench path that could matter: a later parent's image merging into an earlier child's curve (NUM-9, _image_chains/merge_manifolds/refine). I instrumented this by snapshotting every child's point array and _bridge_test_point when its own parent's iterate_bridge returned, and comparing at filter time. 0 changes in 611 children on nested_outer x11 (76 too-close drops, sibling test exercised), 47 on the p3 fixture x3, 67 on k28 x5 and 79 on k32 x5.
  (c) with the pip forgotten, so the exemption is inert, the per-step kept / too-close id lists are identical on base and branch for all four calls.

GOOD:
- _pip_orbits is short and named for the maths, composes +1 links as Trellis._pip_orbit_cuts does, and is used twice.
- The if/elif keeps a single kept path with no duplicated branch.
- The docstrings now say what the guard is (a cost guard) and fix the old 'sibling only' wording.
- The new law pins no number, and break 4 shows the '== sorted' form is the one that bites.
- The TE added a real guard for rubric 8's ordering, which reading alone had covered.

MINOR, not graded:
- The test-side orbit composition appears three times: cases._pip_depth, test_blast_pip_orbit._pip_orbit and test_blast_proximity_guard._pip_orbit. The two test helpers could import cases._pip_depth's logic or share one helper.
- scripts/henon_blast_period_3.py fails on base and branch alike (stale pinned pip id 12), so section 5's 'its numbers go in the report' could not be met. This predates the change.
